# ADR-0098 — the panel's coverage of one claim

Shipped: a seat replays **k = 4** intervals (`PALW_FP_SEAT_INTERVAL_SAMPLES_V1`); the panel is **5** seats with a quorum of **3** (`PALW_V2_PANEL_SEATS` / `PALW_V2_PANEL_QUORUM`, both presets). A licensing object is carried as soon as the quorum's `Valid` receipts pool and a seat's duty ends with it, so between **3** and **5** seats replay a claim before it is licensed — both are tabled. Interval count: the dense A16 and BASE-0 families checkpoint every decode call, so a claim of D decode tokens has **N = max(1, D − 1)** intervals; the hybrid checkpoints at `n_ctx`, so its claims have **N = 1** and every seat replays the whole job. Measured over **5000** beacons per row, with the draw the seats run.

## 1. The forger's best lie — one token, caught only by replaying its own interval

A lie the cache never records (the selected token, or the last layer's work after its K/V rows) is found only by a seat
whose draw includes its interval. `closed` is `1 − ((N − k)/N)^s`; `measured` is the mean over intervals and, after the
slash, the least-drawn interval (the forger's best place). The last column is how many such forged claims a producer files
before the chance that one is caught reaches 90 %.

D = 300 is the claim testnet-11 licensed on 2026-09-05 (N = 299; each of its three seats replayed four intervals); D = 512 is the dense row's whole window; D = 1024 is the free-prompt decode ceiling. The measured minimum is the least-drawn of N intervals over 5000 beacons, so it sits below the closed form by the binomial spread — one standard deviation is 0.35 points at N = 299, s = 5 — and not by a bias: `palw_seat_coverage_v1`'s test holds every interval within six deviations of the closed form.

## 2. A lie the cache records — caught by ANY later draw, through the state root

Before replaying interval j a seat recomputes the cache up to j and compares its root with the committed one, so a lie that alters the cache is caught by a seat whose draw includes its interval or any later one: `1 − (C(i, k) / C(N, k))^s`. At N = 299, s = 5:

| interval i | closed | measured |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 100.00 % | 100.00 % |
| 74 | 100.00 % | 100.00 % |
| 149 | 100.00 % | 100.00 % |
| 224 | 99.70 % | 99.70 % |
| 269 | 88.07 % | 87.48 % |
| 289 | 49.53 % | 49.92 % |
| 298 | 6.51 % | 6.90 % |

The forger's best cache-altering lie is therefore at the last interval, where the number is section 1's. **Today this path is discarded**: a seat whose recomputed root differs files nothing and records nothing (ADR-0098 §1.3, fixed by Decision 2).

## 4. The capture arm's leaf sample, for comparison

A seat checking a served capture opens leaf 0 and then three leaves drawn uniformly (`fp_capture_samples_clear`). Its
chance of landing on one forged leaf, for claims of the dense graph-v5 row at their real leaf counts:

| job (prompt / decode) | step leaves | one seat (3 draws) | five seats (15 draws) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 / 8 | 1697248 | 1 in 565750 | 1 in 113150 |
| 51 / 64 | 12959936 | 1 in 4319979 | 1 in 863996 |
| 51 / 300 | 41757600 | 1 in 13919200 | 1 in 2783840 |
| 200 / 300 | 57105792 | 1 in 19035264 | 1 in 3807053 |

The arm runs only for a capture that fits the 16 MiB material cap. Today a seat whose interval openings have not arrived yet reaches it in the same round, so for such a claim this — not section 1 — can be the seat's whole check (§1.3, named in Decision 6).

## 5. Seats that hold a shard — the stratified panel

Every seat holds one shard and is drawn for it; a claim is licensed when every shard has its own quorum of 3. A one-leaf lie lives in one shard and only that shard's seats can replay it, so the coverage is section 1's at s = seats per shard, whatever the shard count. The per-seat artifact is the Kimi K3 stand-in's parameter count over the shards, at one byte a weight (a floor).

| shards | seat's artifact (≥) | panel seats (5 / shard) | licensing receipts | licensing bytes | one standard transaction (120000 B)? | one-lie coverage, N = 299 |

The widest shard count whose per-shard quorum licenses in one standard transaction is **8**.

## 6. The expected cost of a lie

A conviction slashes exactly the claim's reservation (`void_and_slash`), so the producer's expected cost of one forged leaf, when detection leads to a conviction, is the section 1 number times `claim.reserved`: **6.51 %** of it on the 300-token claim with five replaying seats, **3.96 %** with three. The chain deters a false answer worth less than that; a false answer worth more is deterred only by the challenge window's watchdog, which re-runs every licensed claim and needs the whole model to do it.
